habitat: Broad-leaved woodland, including miombo and mopane, with light leaf litter. SABAP1 says that in the Transvaal lowveld it uses sandveld and mixed woodland and is absent from mopane. It is a breeding migrant, mostly September to February.
summary: A breeding migrant. The male has a broad white band across otherwise black primaries. In the breeding season he grows a long second primary, the pennant, which can reach twice the body length and is dropped or broken off soon after breeding. The female plumage was not described in the texts used. SABAP1 says most birds occur from September to February.

similar.note: Fiery-necked Nightjar shares broad-leaved woodland but has no breeding pennant. The male Pennant-winged Nightjar shows a white band across black primaries and, in the breeding season, the long pennant.

calls.description: No call was described in the Wikipedia or SABAP1 texts consulted. The file is a grade A call from Mutinondo, Zambia, and the filename says it is a male flight call.

research.note: Newman has no page. Wikipedia and SABAP1 give no total length, so size is omitted. Months are September to February. SABAP1 says a few birds may overwinter, but that needs confirmation, so winter months were not added. The female plumage was not described. The pennant is stored as the breeding-male difference. The call text is a gap. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
